headline: Strong underwriting and record investment income lift profit
summary_short: Travelers' Q3 2026 net income was $1.92B ($9.04/share, +10% y/y) and core income $1.95B ($9.18/share, +13%); the combined ratio improved to 86.8%.
summary_long: Core income rose $80M y/y on higher favorable prior-year reserve development of $234M and record pre-tax net investment income of $1.10B, partly offset by catastrophe losses of $538M from wind and hail storms. The underlying combined ratio was 84.1%. Net written premiums were flat at $11.48B, or up 2% excluding the divested Canadian business. Core return on equity was 22.1%. Travelers returned $1.77B to shareholders, including $1.51B of buybacks. The release gives no numeric guidance.
confidence_notes: Core income excludes net realized investment gains and losses. The prior-year quarter's net written premiums included $240M from Canadian operations divested in Q1 2026. Favorable reserve development includes a $295M asbestos reserve addition. Page title shows 'September 30, 2026'; the release is dated October 16, 2026.

drivers.explanation: Higher net favorable prior year reserve development and higher net investment income, partly offset by higher catastrophe losses; fewer shares after buybacks also helped per-share results.
Higher favorable reserve development improved the ratio by 1.9 points, partly offset by 1.2 points from catastrophes and 0.2 points from the underlying ratio.
A higher yield and growth in average invested assets in the long-term fixed income portfolio.
CEO cited very strong underwriting across all three segments and a record investment result.
